p: It is the day on which the Torah was given.
We have already spoken about this
from the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
it is written "an assembly to Hashem your God" (Devarim 16:8),
and it is written "an assembly shall it be for you" (Bamidbar 29:35);
half of it for Hashem and half of it for you,
or all of it for Hashem, etc.,
Now in truth the two pesukim were stated
Regarding the seventh day of Pesach
it says "shall it be for you."
they learned through a gezeirah shavah
to apply what is said of this one to that one.
the mitzvah lies specifically upon the outer garment,
from the pleasures of this world in actual fact,
by eating the bread of affliction.
which is the season of our rejoicing,
that is, upon the outer garment
there should be the aspect of "for you."
And this is the purpose of the derivation
to apply what is said of this one to that one:
meaning that the body too should enjoy
and feel vitality from the kedushah
as it does from the matters of this world;
and on the festival of Shemini Atzeres
the "for you" should also be "for Hashem,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם כׇּל הֲנָאוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
meaning that all the pleasures of this world as well
should be solely for Hashem alone.
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה:
that the "for you" should also be "for Hashem";
It is the day on which the Torah was given.
For through the power of the Torah
upon all the creations in this world,
is only to do the will of their Maker,
as it says in the Gemara (Chullin 7a)
"I am going to do the will of my Maker,"
that is, without any free choice on its part.
And just as it was in this aspect
״אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט),
and the delights of this world
מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, טז).
of every tree of the garden you may surely eat" (Bereishis 2:16).
And with this we will also understand
that it was a fast over a dream,
and therefore even on Shabbos and Yom Tov,
it is permitted to sit in fasting,
regarding which the term "feasting" is used;
eating itself is reckoned as a fast,
"as though he fasted on the ninth," etc.;
the time when the Torah was given,
of the intent of a fast,
that "the diminishing of my fat and blood should be
as though I had offered a korban."
And this is found stated explicitly
regarding the eating of talmidei chachamim:
one who brings a gift to a talmid chacham
is as though he offered bikkurim (Kesubos 105b);
and one who wishes to pour a libation of wine
שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַיִן (יוֹמָא עא, א);
״אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים עוֹבֵר עָלֵינוּ תָּמִיד״ (מְלָכִים ב ד, ט),
"a man of God passes by us continually" (Melachim II 4:9),
whoever hosts a talmid chacham in his home
is as though he offered the daily korbanos.
even a fast over a dream is forbidden,
